questions.stem: An audit list is declared `class AuditList extends ArrayList<String>` and overrides only `add(String)`, adding one to a counter before calling `super.add`. An empty AuditList receives `addAll(List.of("p1", "p2", "p3", "p4"))`. What does the counter read?

options.text: 4, since ArrayList's addAll hands each element to add, which the subclass counts
options.says: ArrayList overrides addAll with an array copy and never calls add

options.text: 4, since a call through super still reaches the subclass's add for each element
options.says: a call through super does reach overrides, but ArrayList's addAll makes no call to add for it to reach

options.text: 0, since ArrayList's addAll copies the elements in without calling add
options.says: ArrayList.addAll uses System.arraycopy, so a counter that trusts add misses every batch

options.text: 0, since code that runs inside the superclass never reaches a subclass's overrides
options.says: a self-call from superclass code is a virtual call and does reach the override, as HashSet's addAll shows

origin.section: Counting Only in add Fixes HashSet and Breaks ArrayList: the Count Follows Code the Subclass Can't See

questions.stem: A class extends a forwarding class that passes every `Set` call to a wrapped set, and overrides only `add`, counting before it forwards. It wraps a new `HashSet`, and a caller passes three new elements to the wrapper's `addAll`. What does the count read?

options.text: 3, since the HashSet's addAll calls add for each element, which the count sees
options.says: the HashSet's addAll calls the HashSet's own add; the wrapper is a different object

options.text: 3, since the addAll it inherits loops over its own overridden add
options.says: the inherited addAll forwards the whole batch to the wrapped set's addAll; it never loops over add

options.text: 0, since the HashSet's addAll calls its own add, never the one in the wrapper
options.says: the wrapped set's internal calls stay on the wrapped set, so a batch is counted only if the wrapper's addAll counts it

options.text: 0, since a wrapper sees only single-element calls and has no way to count a batch
options.says: the wrapper can count a batch by overriding addAll, as InstrumentedSet does

origin.section: A Forwarding Wrapper Counts Each Element Once over Any Set, Because the Set's Own Calls Stay Inside It

questions.stem: A forwarding class implements `Map<String, Integer>` by passing every `Map` method to a wrapped `HashMap`, and declares nothing else. A wrapper holding `{"x"=1}` is compared with `Map.of("x", 1)` both ways: `wrapper.equals(plain)` and `plain.equals(wrapper)`. What do the two calls return?

options.text: true and true, since both sides compare the mappings through the forwarded Map methods
options.says: javac doesn't require equals and hashCode, because Object already implements them; the wrapper keeps Object's identity check

options.text: false and false, since both sides compare object identity rather than the mappings
options.says: the plain map compares mappings through the Map methods, which the wrapper forwards, so that side says true

options.text: false and true, since the wrapper compares identity and the plain map compares mappings
options.says: the wrapper inherits Object.equals, while Map.of's equals checks for a Map with the same mappings, so the answer depends on which side is asked

options.text: true and false, since the wrapper compares mappings and the plain map compares identity
options.says: Map.equals accepts any Map with the same mappings; it is the wrapper, inheriting Object.equals, that compares identity

origin.section: javac Makes a Forwarding Class Implement Set's Methods, Not equals and hashCode

questions.stem: A price cache is `class PriceCache extends LinkedHashMap<String, Long>` and overrides `put`: after `super.put` it removes the eldest key whenever the size passes 100. It does not override anything else. At start-up an empty PriceCache receives `putAll` of a map with 250 entries. How many entries does it hold afterwards?

options.text: 100, since putAll inserts each entry through put, which trims the map
options.says: putAll inserts through HashMap's internal method and never calls put

options.text: 100, since LinkedHashMap itself drops its eldest entry once it grows past its limit
options.says: LinkedHashMap drops entries only when removeEldestEntry returns true, and its default returns false

options.text: 250, since putAll inserts the entries without calling put
options.says: HashMap.putAll goes to an internal insert, so an override of put never runs; removeEldestEntry is the hook putAll is documented to call

options.text: 250, since an override of put applies only to callers holding a PriceCache reference
options.says: overrides are chosen by the object's class, not the reference type; putAll simply never calls put

origin.section: Extend a Class Through the Hook It Documents: LinkedHashMap Calls removeEldestEntry from put and putAll
